note: Attacker-controlled bytes are wrapped as a JSON byte string and passed into the decoder.
The fuzzer decodes the input as a Variant, so nested JSON can instantiate heap-backed built-in types.
Variant decoding can unwrap ExtensionObjects and recursively decode the embedded body as another concrete type.
The unwrapped body is heap-allocated as the concrete decoded type, creating ownership that later cleanup must release exactly once.
A crafted body can also drive nested DiagnosticInfo decoding, which allocates an inner string member that is later freed through the generic clear path.
Cleanup of DiagnosticInfo frees the additionalInfo string and then recursively clears the inner diagnostic info, so any alias to the same heap buffer becomes dangling.
String_clear releases the heap buffer backing the JSON-decoded string, which is the first free in the use-after-free chain.
The generic clear dispatcher walks the decoded object graph and invokes the nested frees on the attacker-controlled structure.
Recursive cleanup can revisit nested diagnostic info after the outer string has already been freed, exposing stale references if the decoder created aliasing.
A second access to the same string storage during recursive cleanup is the memory-safety sink, matching the reported heap-use-after-free read.
